# bugs #3973: String literals that initialize void pointers or integers are emitted as bytes of a host address

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3973/
- Category: [Analyzed, not fixed](../../unresolved.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Keep open. The cause is in printIvalPtr and printIvalType in src/SDCCglue.c. No patch is offered.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The test case of the ticket was compiled with `-c` on r17176 for mcs51, stm8, and z80. For mcs51
it was compiled with the small model and with the options of the ticket. In every case the compiler
writes output of the form that the ticket shows. The `const char *` field gets the address of the
string. The `const void *` field and the `uint32_t` field get literal bytes. For mcs51 with the
small model they were `40 11 62` and `40 11 62 4a` in one run and `40 91 a1` and `40 91 a1 f1` in
the next.

The bytes are the low bytes of an address in the compiler's own memory. In a run of the compiler
under gdb, the value that `printIvalPtr` printed had the name `__str_0`, the storage class
`S_LITERAL`, and the `v_char` member `0x55a9d50d9fe0`, which pointed to the characters. In that
run the compiler wrote `e0 9f 0d` and `e0 9f 0d d5`. The author of the second comment takes the
bytes for the characters of the string, which would be `41 41 41`.

A file that contains only `const void * const only_void = "BBB";` gets three such bytes for mcs51,
and the string is absent from its assembly.

## Known

The explanation was read from the source of r17176 and was not tested with a patch.
`constExprValue` in `src/SDCCast.c` returns for a string literal a value that has the storage
class `S_LITERAL` and the label of the string as its name. In the union of the value, the numeric
members overlap `v_char`, the compiler's pointer to the characters. Code that takes the value for a
number reads that pointer.

`printIvalPtr` in `src/SDCCglue.c` calls `printIvalCharPtr`, which prints the label, only when the
pointer in the declaration points to a character type or to an unsigned `int` type of any length.
For every other pointer type, `const void *` among them, `printIvalPtr` executes its `IS_LITERAL`
branch and prints the bytes of the value with `aopLiteral`.

For the `uint32_t` field, `list2val` in `src/SDCCval.c` removes the cast and returns the value of
the string literal. `printIvalType` converts it with `valCastLiteral` and prints the result.

`printIvalCharPtr` is also the only function that adds the string to `ccpStr`, the set that
`emitStaticSeg` consults before it emits a string. A string to which no character pointer refers
is not emitted, as the file with `only_void` shows.

The ports share these functions, except pic14, which has copies of them in `src/pic14/glue.c`. The
third comment has output of the same form for mos6502. Neither port was tested.

## Open

A fix needs about 20 lines in `src/SDCCglue.c`. `printIvalPtr` has to pass every value whose
symbol is a string literal to `printIvalCharPtr`. `printIvalType` has to print the address of the
string by its label, as its branch for values from `initPointer` does, and it has to add the string
to `ccpStr`. This outline was not implemented.

One point needs a decision for mcs51. The `initPointer` branch of `printIvalType` writes zero to
every byte above the two address bytes. An integer that is initialized from a code address would
therefore not get the `0x80` byte that a generic pointer to code has.

- local 0001 is the `printIvalPtr` case of this ticket with a wide string literal and an
